explanation: The OK hand sign (thumb and index finger forming a circle) doesn't carry a documented negative or vulgar meaning in India, unlike in parts of the Middle East, the Mediterranean, or Brazil. The same hand shape appears in Indian corporate logos (including Piramal Group, Bharat Petroleum, and Adlabs Studios) and echoes the vitarka mudra, a teaching/explanation gesture from Buddhist and Hindu iconography, both of which point to a neutral-to-positive reading rather than an offensive one.
local_tip: Using the OK hand sign to mean 'fine' or 'got it' is generally safe in India; if you want to be extra clear, you can also just say 'theek hai' (okay) or nod.
